addition.item: **Menu Dialog: Cards**: the mobile menu (and the menu dialog, if used) with rounded menu items, the active one in the theme's primary colour, and a round close button above the menu.
**Scroll Progress**: a thin bar in the primary colour at the top of the window that fills as visitors scroll, on all pages or on articles only.

**Button** at the end of the header or navbar, with its own link, style (primary, secondary, default), new window option, and optionally in the mobile header. Its text can be a language string, so it can be translated with language overrides.

fix.item: With *Blend with page content* (transparent header), the glass or solid surface is left out: the blend inverted its colours. Menu style, dropdowns and the button stay.

addition.item: Show the glass or solid navbar **Always**, not only while sticky: a floating capsule from the top of the page, with space and a shadow below it. Works without a sticky navbar.

**Menu Style**: Pill (rounded item, the active one in the theme's primary colour, or white on dark tints) or Underline (a line growing from the middle on hover). Items keep their height, so dropdowns stay where they are.
**Dropdowns: Glass**: rounded, see-through dropdowns with a soft shadow and rounded items.
A divider between the menu and the modules after it, such as a language switcher.
Menu style, dropdowns and divider also work without a glass or solid navbar.

change.item: Field labels: Header Pro Style, Show, Shape, Tint, Effects.

addition.item: Sticky Style in the customizer under Header: while the navbar is sticky it becomes frosted glass or a solid bar, full width or a floating capsule.
Tint from the theme: its background, muted, primary or secondary colour, so it follows the style chosen in the customizer. Menu text turns light on dark tints.

Opacity, blur, capsule gap and corners, shadow, border, and a smaller navbar height while sticky. Applies to the mobile header too, unless switched off; a static mobile navbar then becomes sticky like the desktop one.
Falls back to a nearly solid bar in browsers without backdrop blur, and skips the transitions when visitors prefer reduced motion.
